note: Closest profile in this batch to the stated ICP, and it fails on the one criterion the ICP cares most about. Matches successful: a business owner, confirmed from the application by the rep — 'I saw in the application that you run your own company, correct?' — with management work, driving and site visits. Matches neglected_health on the same reading applied to the Francisco Vega assessment: health is unambiguously the neglected area of an otherwise functioning life, degraded over a decade of 70% seated days rather than by any acute event. It is close to the edge of 'not a crisis' — a compressed disc, a subluxing knee and hypertension at 105 kg are real pathology — but the presentation is accumulated neglect, not emergency. Matches not_deconditioned, again by the Vega precedent: he is roughly 15 kg above his own target rather than the 50 lb the exclusion names, and critically he is not gym-averse, which is the operative half of that criterion — he trained heavily last year, bought kettlebells on his own initiative and had already started before the call. Misses good_to_great, and decisively: he is not moving from good to great, he is trying to get back to where he was 14 to 16 years ago. 'Where I would like to land, to have like around 90 kilos... I can remember myself when I was having 90 kilos.' That is rescue, and his own framing confirms it — 'I want to just start with a new lifestyle, new mode.' The income criterion is deliberately in neither list: no financial discussion occurred anywhere in the recorded portion, so affordability is unverified rather than passed or failed. Edge rather than core on the good_to_great miss alone; if income later proves out, this is the profile the ICP was written for in every respect except starting point, which suggests the good_to_great criterion is the one doing the most work to exclude otherwise ideal buyers. Judged on criteria, not outcome — and the outcome is in any case unknown, since the recording is truncated at 00:18:24 before any offer.
